reviews.review: The game is awesome rn its just not complete cant wait to see more

This game is a true pillar of design understanding.
The developers clearly understand and respect what their game is and mold every facet of the game around its identity.
I have found little to no flaws with this game and I am simply getting more excited the more I play it rather than less.
How this game is not more popular I do not understand.
If you like risk of rain, gunfire reborn, and similar roguelites you simply must play this.

As someone who hates playing roguelikes with a passion (just not my cup o' tea), roguelites strike a wonderful balance and this one especially is an absolute blast! And yet it falls closer to roguelikes in essence, as the progression doesn't so much as make you more powerful, and they open up more freedom and choice in how you progress. Getting farther with each run requires the same careful observation and learning as true roguelikes, but progression in Roboquest makes it easier to experiment with different builds and playstyles, as well as more likely that you'll be able to put together something cohesive with each run.

I'm usually pretty reluctant to buy into Early Access games, but this one looked too fun to pass up, and I don't regret it one bit! Ryseup Studios is very active in development and publicly active with the community, which gives me a huge amount of confidence and faith in the final product, not only that it'll actually see the light of day, but also that it'll be an excellent result of both developer vision and valued player feedback. Each update brings substantial and (usually) positive changes, and I'm beyond stoked to see where this goes!

And now for some pros, cons, and wait-and-sees!

Pros:
- Stellar gameplay, both gunplay and mobility (with one major caveat there). It's super smooth and feels amazingly responsive
- Guns, perks, and viable playstyles are wonderfully varied and so much fun to experiment with. Obviously, there's room to improve, as some guns are obvious powerhouses while others feel weak, but that should hopefully get smoothed out over development before final release
- The art direction and overall the little touches are gorgeous and really cute. The onamonapeia effects are fun, and you can make your hoverbus jump on loading screens with the space bar! What little we've seen of the characters are endearing, and nothing is more fun than seeing your co-op partner constantly referred to as your Brobot

Cons:
- As is expected of an actively developed Early Access game, the enemy balance is rough and constantly changing, sometimes for better and sometimes for worse. Some enemies have frustrating attacks that are nearly impossible to dodge or deal insane damage. This will, again, hopefully be ironed out by the time it fully launches, but for now it's pretty tough and annoying
- There are some input issues, such as times when my mouse clicks just don't register
- Mobility, as smooth as it is during combat, is still touchy and incredibly frustrating during certain challenge rooms. When you're trying complex platforming with a floor of lava and tons of damaging environmental factors, issues like touchy midair control and the lack of sprint persistence when landing after a jump just piss you off and can ruin an otherwise perfect run. I'm getting really good at combat, but those challenge rooms still murder me
- Co-op is super fun and helps a ton in progression with the revive system, but every time I've played co-op, the off-host player's game will crash eventually. We can usually get a few runs in, even to the end of current content, but it's still pretty annoying when it happens during a great run

Wait-and-sees:
- I realize I already mentioned enemy balance as a con, but it really is a work in progress, and we'll probably see it improve over time, especially with how active Ryse is with the community
- Story and lore: so far, there's just been a couple cute comic-style cutscenes after bosses with some world-building, but hopefully we'll see some really compelling character arcs, and the awesome relationship between Max and her Guardian!
- The soundtrack is fun and bouncy, but it's also very limited and repetitive so far. I'm really looking forward to seeing it expanded and integrated better with the overall game!

So yeah, my verdict is hell yeah, this game is well worth it to any fans of fast-paced FPS games! It stops just short of being frenetic, and even in the Early Access stage is already an impressively polished game and I'm stoked to see how much better it can get

You guys got this, Ryseup!

Doom 2016's fast paced arcade arena play mixed with Warframe's slide boost movement, add some rails to grind, good double jump gravity, and simple but well-made roguelite mechanics make this an amazing hidden gem. It's compared to Gunfire Reborn a lot, but aside from being roguelite FPS, they are vastly different. 

2 Player COOP on Heroic Difficulty is insanely fun and I can't wait to see what the devs bring next.
